title: Korea to Extend AI Labeling Duty to YouTubers, Other Users
key_facts: South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT is drafting an amendment to the Framework Act on the Development of AI and Establishment of a Foundation of Trust (AI Framework Act), according to industry officials on the 8th (8 Oct 2026).
The current law requires AI companies to disclose visibly and clearly that deepfake content, AI output hard to distinguish from reality, was made by AI.
Under the plan, AI users who produce or distribute deepfake content would insert watermarks themselves.
The government has suspended fines for violations until at least 22 Jan next year (2027) to limit disruption for the industry.
A senior official says AI cannot reliably tell which outputs count as deepfakes, so companies make every label visible to comply.
Officials see little room to extend the watermarking duty beyond January because deepfake abuse is spreading, including voice phishing and sex offences.
The scope of users' obligations is still under discussion.
quote_evidence: The Ministry of Science and ICT is drafting an amendment to the Framework Act on the Development of AI and Establishment of a Foundation of Trust, known as the AI Framework Act
The government has suspended fines for violations until at least Jan. 22 next year to limit disruption for the industry.

why_it_matters_hint: Ordinary creators, not only AI firms, may soon be legally responsible for marking AI-made fakes in South Korea.
event_date: Officials spoke on 8 Oct 2026; article published 11 Oct 2026.
